# Phase Three — 34 Final Revelations Before Source Writes

The Awtsmoos renews the plan as He renews the frame; Awtsmoos.com demands the last critique before implementation earns its name.

1. A canonical protocol needs explicit protocol/version fields everywhere, including translators.
2. Canonical duration must never default silently when validating AI output.
3. Resolution, fps, orientation and safe area belong at movie level.
4. Scene time and layer-local time need separately documented coordinate spaces.
5. Keyframe `at` is layer-local and must fit effective layer duration.
6. Camera semantics must survive projection even when a 2D editor cannot render a true camera.
7. Hybrid scenes must not collapse to 3D merely because one layer has depth.
8. Characters should reference stable cast IDs instead of duplicating persona definitions.
9. Charts need semantic data as well as visual styles so editors can re-author them.
10. Paths and patches need explicit geometry, not screenshot-only representations.
11. Particles require deterministic seed/count/emitter fields.
12. Text needs safe-area metadata for portrait and mobile outputs.
13. Adapters need stable IDs for round-trip edit handoff.
14. Unsupported layers must be preserved in projection metadata, never silently ignored.
15. Capability profiles must name dimensions, semantic layers and strengths separately.
16. The AI contract should include field examples while remaining JSON-safe.
17. Structured intent templates must distribute timing from requested duration, never hard-code 60 or 120 seconds.
18. Three-minute proof must assert exact 180-second canonical duration.
19. Acceptance scenes collectively include every major semantic layer kind.
20. Acceptance cameras include wide, close, overhead/angle, orbit/dolly/crane variants.
21. Characters appear in multiple scenes, not merely metadata.
22. Infographics animate data-oriented visuals, not just labels.
23. Tutorial scenes contain ordered visual steps and callouts.
24. Narrative scenes contain cast/action progression.
25. 2D and 3D particles are both represented.
26. Rendering samples deterministic movie time independent of wall-clock playback.
27. Acceptance may render at 12fps while production APIs still allow higher fps.
28. Export success is not proof until the resulting file is readable by ffprobe.
29. Duration success is not visual proof until distant frame witnesses differ.
30. Mobile UI success needs a narrow viewport and practical touch targets.
31. Concurrent agents make stale reads dangerous; hash-gate every existing-file rewrite.
32. New compatibility modules are safer than deleting peer prototypes during active work.
33. Completion documentation must identify the canonical path so future agents stop spawning duplicate cores.
34. If an app cannot consume the full movie, that limitation belongs in capabilities and fidelity reports rather than marketing language.
